etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English, past participle of passen (“to pass, to go by”), whence Modern English pass.

definitions.definition: The period of time that has already happened, in contrast to the present and the future.

quote.text: The past, at least, is secure.

quote.citation: 1860, Richard Chenevix Trench, On the English Language, Past and Present:
quote.text: The present is only intelligible in the light of the past, often a very remote past indeed.

quote.citation: 2012, Chinle Miller, In Mesozoic Lands: The Mesozoic Geology of Arches and Canyonlands National Parks, Kindle edition:
quote.text: The Mesozoic landscape of southeastern Utah can tell us much about the past, and it's one of the most intriguing and beautiful landscapes on Earth.

definitions.definition: Having already happened; in the past; finished. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 7, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:
quote.text: The highway to the East Coast which ran through the borough of Ebbfield had always been a main road and even now, despite the vast garages, the pylons and the gaily painted factory glasshouses which had sprung up beside it, there still remained an occasional trace of past cultures.

definitions.definition: (postmodifier) Following expressions of time to indicate how long ago something happened; ago. [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: 1999, George R.R. Martin, A Clash of Kings, Bantam, published 2011, page 538:
quote.text: That had been, what, three years past?

quote.citation: 2009, John Sadler, Glencoe, Amberley, published 2009, page 20:
quote.text: Some four decades past, as a boy, I had a chance encounter and conversation with the late W.A. Poucher [...].

definitions.definition: Of a period of time: having just gone by; previous. [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: 2012 April 23, Angelique Chrisafis, “François Hollande on top but far right scores record result in French election”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: Sarkozy's total will be seen as a personal failure. It is the first time an outgoing president has failed to win a first-round vote in the past 50 years and makes it harder for Sarkozy to regain momentum.

definitions.definition: (grammar) Of a tense, expressing action that has already happened or a previously-existing state. [from 18th c.]
(time) Any number of minutes after the last hour

quote.citation: 2012 April 22, Sam Sheringham, “Liverpool 0-1 West Brom”, in BBC Sport‎[2]:
quote.text: But they were stunned when Glen Johnson's error let in Peter Odemwingie to fire past Pepe Reina on 75 minutes.

definitions.definition: Having recovered or moved on from (a traumatic experience, etc.).
Passing by, especially without stopping or being delayed.
(obsolete) simple past and past participle of pass

quote.citation: 1632, John Vicars, The XII Aeneids of Virgil:
quote.text: Great Tuscane dames, as she their towns past by, / Wisht her their daughter-in-law, but frustrately.
